deployment_name: oncology-coscientist (barlowa124/oncology-coscientist @ e680759, research prototype - not a clinical deployment)

DA-01.note: README limits the system to public retrospective TCGA data and states results reflect the dataset, not any clinical use. No regulatory classification exists or was sought. This is correct for a research tool, but any clinical framing is blocked.

DA-02.note: The approval gate is a technical control: approve() refuses when the report bytes or the agent_run hash changed since render, and the API returns 409 on tamper. No production case sample exists to demonstrate observed enforcement.

DA-03.note: Approvals record reviewer identity and an optional note, but nothing measures whether the reviewer engaged with the content versus rubber-stamping.

DA-04.note: Run records are content-addressed: config_sha256 binds the config, the report embeds the agent_run sha, final_report_sha256 pins the rendered bytes, and approval/rejection is recorded on the run record. The verifier recomputes hashes before any decision is accepted.

DA-05.note: agent replay re-executes a recorded run; agent_run.json plus hashed report and results artifacts allow end-to-end reconstruction of a specific run on demand.

DA-06.note: Models are evaluated on held-out splits and checks abstain a model when integrity fails, but performance is characterized per cohort, not per clinically meaningful subgroup.

DA-07.note: No production drift monitoring with thresholds and response exists. The system is run on demand against fixed snapshots.
DA-07.evidence_reference: absent by inspection of oncocs/; no monitoring module

DA-08.note: Every run binds code and config through git_sha and config_sha256, so the change history is auditable, but there are no approved change records or a documented change-control workflow.

DA-09.note: Replay can recompute a past decision, but no per-update backward-compatibility check compares decisions across model versions.
DA-09.evidence_reference: oncocs/agents/replay.py exists; no cross-version comparison harness

DA-10.note: The recorded LLM backend replays responses keyed by prompt sha256, so a past decision re-derives deterministically without a live model.

DA-11.note: No defined path from an AI-related error to containment, CAPA, or regulatory reporting exists. Defects are handled informally through git.
DA-11.evidence_reference: absent by inspection; no incident/CAPA procedure in repo

DA-12.note: No reviewer training material on the system's known failure modes or limitations exists.
DA-12.evidence_reference: absent by inspection; no training artifact in repo

DA-13.note: The agent runs a local Ollama model whose model_id is recorded per run; there is no vendor change-notification or data-handling contract because the model is local and open-weight. Version pinning remains informal.

DA-14.note: Path-traversal probes, encoded-segment probes, and hash-tamper tests exist against the API and CLI. No adversarial-input suite targets the model or retrieval layer.

DA-15.note: The system produces survival-cohort statistics and PDQ-corpus retrieval summaries; no in-silico or virtual-organ model output supports any conclusion, so this item is out of scope for this artifact.

DA-16.note: No production usage monitoring against a validated population exists; out-of-envelope use is possible and unmonitored.
DA-16.evidence_reference: absent by inspection; no envelope/usage monitor

DA-17.note: A failing run check abstains the affected model rather than passing partial data through. The approval path refuses hash-mismatched artifacts. Failure modes are visible, not silent.
DA-17.evidence_reference: oncocs/checks.py module contract; approve.py hash refusal

DA-18.note: Prompts, split definitions, rag doc ids, and inference settings live in cohort config files hashed as config_sha256 on every run. Prompt-side keys excluded from the hash (e.g. rag_mode) are enumerated explicitly in config.py.

DA-19.note: Each run is a separate content-addressed record so repeated submissions do not overwrite. No design retains or compares the sequence of outputs for anchoring review.
DA-19.evidence_reference: agents/approve.py per-run records; no sequence view

DA-20.note: Runs carry model_id and config hashes so every record a model version touched is enumerable. No re-review workflow exists to act on that enumeration.

DA-21.note: The recorded backend lets runs proceed without the live model. No documented manual fallback procedure defines degraded operation.

DA-22.note: Download, harmonization, and split code are project source under git with input and config hashes recorded per run, so preprocessing is under the same change binding as the model-facing layer.

DA-23.note: The retrieval corpus is a pinned NCI PDQ snapshot whose document ids come from the hashed cohort configs. There is no live currency feed, so the effective revision set is exactly the committed one.

DA-24.note: The rendered report carries an UNAPPROVED banner until the gate stamps the approved banner onto the exact hashed bytes. What reaches the record is the verified output, qualifiers included.

DA-25.note: Artifacts are content-addressed and self-describing, which supports reconstruction. No retention-period design or archival plan exists.
DA-25.evidence_reference: hash-addressed results/ artifacts; no retention design doc
